limits: Helpers precede DQM operations; records denote lifecycle attempts, not hardware-success acknowledgments.
Nested reference-counted evictions need not produce independent hardware save events.
Probe entry interception changes timing and can affect exposure.
No-event cases do not prove no trap or no alternative eviction path.
Module disk SHA/srcversion plus runtime symbol availability bind code version; no attestation of every live patched instruction is claimed.
All static/dynamic events retained and target PID/GPU classified offline.
BOOTTIME per-call markers are in producer journal; ftrace contains run markers. No container tracefs mount or relay process.
No /dev/kfd observer subscription, no SMI FIFO, no driver reset/reload.
Text ftrace timestamps may be rounded to microseconds; preserve at least ±1 microsecond uncertainty for interval boundary classification.
Per-call interval brackets host native launch entry through synchronization return, not exact GPU execution or trap time.
Probe profile hits exceeding captured trace rows may occur outside capture; all such excesses are explicitly retained and are not silently assigned to a case.
BOOTTIME and MONOTONIC are sampled consecutively; their difference range is diagnostic and includes sampling delay.
Static events with matching process PID lack a complete per-event GPU identity and are reported separately from the scoped helper events.
interpretation: Direct observed association of spontaneous predicted register copies and fresh trap return PCs with target-process SVM queue eviction/restore attempts. Helper entries do not acknowledge hardware context-save completion and do not reconstruct original attempt405 trap history.
